summary: Covering attempt for 9/n: the identities 9/n = 1/a+1/(na) (a=(n+1)/9, n≡8 mod 9) and 9/n = 1/a+2/(na) (a=(n+2)/9, n≡7 mod 9) plus 9/n = 3/(n/3) = 3·1/(n/3) (3|n) cover all n ≤4000 except residues 1,2,4,5 mod 9; the 1778 uncovered n ≤4000 are covered by k-families (k|n(n+k)/9, k≤199) for 914 of them, leaving 864 (e.g. 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 13, 19). Completeness of {2,5,11,19} is therefore NOT proved; the covering needs divisor conditions in classes 1,2,4,5 mod 9.
not_done: The divisor-condition covering for classes 1,2,4,5 (mod 9) is open in this attempt.
next: Search for a second identity family with a modulus coprime to 9 that covers the 864 leftover n.

summary: The mod-2^k local densities of 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) do not depend on p at all (k=4,5,6): the all-even share is 0.4545 (k=4,5) and 0.4783 (k=6) for every unit class of p, because x→ux gives p→p/u. So the 2-adic local density cannot produce the observed mod-8 split of U8/U4 (0.40 for p≡1 mod 8, 0.55 for p≡5 mod 8): that split is non-local.

summary: Read arXiv:2511.16817 §§1, 3, 4, 6 (HTML rendering): Thm 3.1 (for m≥8, more than exp{c φ(m)^{1/3}/(log m)^{2/3}} exceptional primes) assumes m large in its Type-I/II congruence count (Brun–Titchmarsh uniform in the modulus m·a·d ≤3N); Thm 1.3 (§4) is an upper bound via Vaughan's large sieve (Lemma 4.1 sum f(p)/p ≍ (log x)²/φ(m)); §6 verifies the m-claim numerically for m∈[16,30000] except m=19. So m→∞ enters through the φ(m) growth, the explicit 6.52·10⁹ threshold, and the "assume m large" reduction; nothing in it is claimed for m=4.

Proof: the swap (u,v)↦(v,u) has fixed points u=v with n=u(tu−2), which for prime n forces u∈{1,n} and then t=n+2 ≡3 (4) or t=3/n, neither ≡0 (4) with t≥4; so for every odd prime the swap is fixed-point-free and R(p) is even. Numerically R(n) ≡ #diagonal words (mod 2) for all n≤1e5, and no diagonal word exists at primes ≡1 (4) ≤2e5.
not_done: A second involution on the off-diagonal words was not sought.
next: Look for a second involution on the (u<v) words with computable fixed points.

The divisor criterion (12/M = 1/y+1/z, M=n(n+3), d|M², d≡−M (12), (M²/d+M)≡0 (12)) agrees with the enumerator on 1499/1499 values ≤6000; a mod-3-only criterion agrees on only 1410/1499. summary: Premise false: the ES cubic 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx)w has three A1 nodes at the coordinate points (Gröbner basis; quadratic part discriminant p² ≠ 0); its minimal resolution is a weak del Pezzo surface of degree 3 with Pic ≅ I^{1,6}, in which no nonzero class has D²=0 and K·D=0 (Cauchy–Schwarz). So there is no genus-one fibration to compute ranks on; the pencil x=y=0 splits into a line and a conic.
not_done: Rank computations (no object).
next: Replace by a conic-bundle analysis if a Selmer-type question is wanted.

summary: Residual variance of log U (8966 primes): base (log p, loglog p, log L(1,χ_p)) 0.0480; + Legendre weights q≤47: 0.0454; + log τ((p+3)/4), log τ(p−1): 0.0383; + log h(−4p) too: 0.0373 (total var log U 0.191). The divisor-richness terms explain the largest part of the remaining variance.

Raw residues p mod 5 and p mod 7 have residual correlations +0.05 and +0.07 with the residual log U (|ρ| ≤0.07, as the item says); the Legendre symbols carry the information: (5/p) gives ρ=−0.28, (7/p) gives −0.01.

For p≡3 (4), U correlates positively with L(1,χ_{−p}) = πh(−p)/√p: ρ = +0.57 raw, log-slope +0.41 (n=8993), with the q·β_q Euler pattern of Z0826 (q·β_q = +0.26…+0.51 for q≤31), the opposite sign to p≡1 (4) (slope −0.29; Z0827).

Odd squares m² (m≤599): the median ratio of U(m²) to the median of U at m²±1, m²±2 is 0.06 for prime m and 1.5 for composite m (overall median 0.62). Prime squares are the hard squares (U(p²) ≈ 6% of the neighbourhood), composite odd squares are typical or large — the count-level shadow of T1.
next: Test the prime-square ratio for m up to 2000.

summary: Adding indicators 1[q|p+3] to the Legendre regression gives coefficients +0.05…+0.12 (SE 0.006–0.015) for all q≥5, and the mod-3 gap in q·β_q shrinks from 0.33 to 0.17 (means −0.01/−0.35 before, −0.07/−0.24 after). The full shift structure, 1[q|p+s] for q≤47, s≤12 (168 features), gives no support for β ∝ (−s/q): the sign of the indicator coefficient agrees with the Legendre symbol (−s/q) in only 29 of 68 significant cases.

summary: Local density at odd q of the surface 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx): the count mod q is independent of (p/q) for q=3,…,23 (log ratio exactly 0), because x→ux maps p to p/u. The local density therefore cannot produce the Legendre weights; the observed q·β_q ≈ +0.4 (p≡3 mod 4) and ≈ −0.3 (p≡1) are non-local.

Lemma verified on all 7065 solutions of 4/p (odd primes p≤1000): p divides the largest denominator z. Proof (re-checked, see BRAINSTORM/z52d_pass2_TO3.md §Lemma): x ≤ 3p/4 < p so p∤x; the mod-p reduction gives p|y or p|z; if p∤z then y=pb and the equation forces z = pbx/(ab−x) with a=4x−p, which contradicts the size bounds unless a=1, b=x, which is impossible. Dictionary: p|z only is Type I, p|y and p|z is Type II, and p|y alone never occurs.

Family tests of 241, 2521, 193 (exact solutions): 241 has 8 solutions, all squarefree denominators, primitive, not all denominators free of 3 (it fails the "no denominator divisible by 3" family), no denominator divisible by 4; 193 has 6 solutions, all squarefree, with a denominator divisible by 4; 2521 has 9 solutions with x-divides-z 0. summary: Shift bound: for p≤2e5 the largest greedy shift is 59 (at 118801), no prime with shift ≥112 (consistent with the OEIS-cited bound, which was not re-verified). Derivation: a shift s is achieved at p iff the two-term problem 4s/(p(p+s)) = 1/y+1/z is solvable (x=(p+s)/4); the implication from bounded s to bounded U-certificates was not proved, only compared (Z0943).

Lemma (proved here): a solution with first denominator x=(p+s)/4 exists iff 4s/(p(p+s)) is a sum of two unit fractions; so the shift is a two-term divisor condition, and the U-certificate is a three-term one.

summary: Cleared equation: with x=g·a, y=g·b, gcd(a,b)=1, the equation 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) becomes z = p·g·a·b / (4·g·a·b − p·(a+b)), so the stratum problem is an integrality condition on this denominator. Checked on all 1562 primitive-pair solutions with p≤300: 1562/1562 agree. Combined with the gcd bijection (508/508, p≤300), the strata are scalings of primitive solutions of 4g/p, so the gcd stratification gives no new structure.
